done.why: I poured water into the bucket while standing next to it instead of sitting in it, so it flew up and took the pearl necklace with it. Waiting didn't bring it back. After that, every path I tried looped back to rooms I'd already seen. The ledge says I'm not equipped for it, the other passages are blocked by rockfalls, and the unicorn ran off with the key. My score stayed at 20, so I left.

about: You're an adventurer underground in the Wizard of Frobozz's territory. You walk through a barrow, along a ravine, through a spinning room that scrambles your sense of direction, into a riddle room and a formal garden with a unicorn. You pick up treasures and work out small puzzles with ordinary objects, like using a teapot to carry water to a bucket. All the while a cackling wizard pops up now and then to cast spells at you.

moments.note: 'take the sword too' wasn't understood. I found out I have to talk in plain commands.
Asking a question ('why is the lantern familiar?') got 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.' Questions get nowhere.
The lantern 'would rather not discuss' its last adventure. Charming.
A wizard showed up, said 'Fence!' and disappeared cackling.
An invisible fence blocked me both north and south and nothing explained how long it would last. I waited several times before it went away at turn 28.
'hit the fence with the sword' and 'examine the fence' (turn 25) weren't understood. The fence was blocking me but I couldn't do anything with it.
HELP gave me a clear list of what I can type. Very useful for a newcomer.
The carousel room sends you off in random directions. Disorienting, and that seems to be the point.
I typed 'a well' as the answer to the riddle and the stone door opened with a clap of thunder. That felt great.
'look up' said the ceiling isn't doing anything interesting, but the room description says the roof isn't visible.
I couldn't take my necklace back out of the bucket without climbing in. Odd.
My sword started glowing near the unicorn, a nice hint that something is going on.
Looking at 'the white animal' gave the exact same text as the unicorn. Were they two animals or one?
'You can't look inside a china teapot. The china teapot is empty.' That contradicts itself.
Filling the teapot at the ford just worked the way I hoped.
I poured the water in while standing outside the bucket, and it left without me, taking the necklace.
I grabbed for the key and the unicorn decided I was an 'uncouth sort of vagabond.' Funny.
Every route led back to the carousel. I'd run out of new places.

wished: Ask questions in ordinary words, like 'what did he do to me?' or 'why is my sword glowing?'
Examine or hit the invisible fence, or at least get some sign of how long it would last
Call the bucket back down, or get some hint about how it comes back
Climb onto the ledge with something I could find
Win over the unicorn some gentler way to get the key
Walk toward a thing ('walk toward the glow') instead of naming a compass direction

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: It made me smile and gave me a sense of who I am here.

lines.line: The Wizard, in a deep and resonant voice, speaks the word "Fence!" He then vanishes, cackling gleefully.
lines.why: The first real event. It was funny and a bit worrying.

lines.line: There is a deafening clap of thunder and the stone door quietly swings open to reveal a passageway beyond.
lines.why: My reward for solving the riddle in plain English.

lines.line: What is left reads: o b o at the top, A G I across the middle with E and L beneath, and m p a at the bottom.
lines.why: A mysterious clue I couldn't work out. It made me want to come back to it.

lines.line: The bucket swiftly rises up, and is gone.
lines.why: The moment I realized I should have been inside the bucket.

lines.line: The unicorn, unsurprised by this evidence that you are indeed the uncouth sort of vagabond it suspected you were, melts into the hedges and is gone.
lines.why: The best line in the game: a funny putdown.

fun.why: The riddle, the bucket and the unicorn were fun, but too much time went to waiting out the fence and stumbling through the random carousel.

engagement.why: I wanted to solve the bucket and the etchings. After I lost the bucket and the map looped back on itself, my interest dropped.

difficulty.why: As a newcomer I kept getting 'That sentence isn't one I recognize' for normal phrasing. The fence had no explanation. One wrong move with the bucket left me stuck with no hint about how to recover.

interestingness.why: A wizard who hexes you, a room that spins you around, a riddle door, a unicorn wearing a key. Lots of strange, surprising things.

prose.why: Dry, funny descriptions (the lantern, the unicorn, the tea nobody came to), with a few contradictory lines like the teapot and the ceiling.
